evidence.quote: When `network_policy` is omitted, all outbound traffic is allowed.

plans.name: Public preview
plans.note: Unknown limits are not promises of unlimited capacity.

caveats: Free public preview as of2026-09-28. Homepage lists FUTURE rates that apply when billing goes live; do not mislabel them currently charged. Each sandbox Firecracker,1–8vCPU,512MiB–8GB,10GiB disk,1min–8h timeout.

Features set to null were not verified. No sandbox was purchased or tested; feature/performance statements are documentation claims. Null maximums are unknown unless a cited note explicitly states unlimited.
A complete monthly bill requires known snapshot/egress/plan limits; do not silently treat missing ancillary charges as free.
Preview: currently free; list price not yet charged. The estimate uses the published post-preview rate ($0.0504/vCPU-h, $0.0162/GB-h) from leap0.dev.

Disk is a fixed 10 GiB per sandbox (homepage: "10 GiB disk"); no larger-disk option, disk rate, snapshot storage rate or egress rate is published (leap0.dev and docs llms-full.txt, 2026-09-28), so they stay null.

Preview account cap: max 3 sandboxes per organization (createSandbox returns 409 'sandbox limit reached'); API rate limit 1000 requests/60s; 25 templates and 20 users per org. Raise only by contacting Leap0.

Default sandbox timeout is 5 min (API default 300 s, max 28800 s); on timeout the sandbox is killed unless auto_pause=true, which pauses it into a snapshot (memory+disk). Timeout is wall-clock, not idle-based.

Billing has NOT gone live as of 2026-09-29: homepage still 'Free during public preview — no credit card required. The rates below apply when billing goes live.' No launch date, no plans, no storage/snapshot/egress/stopped-disk rates, no minimum billed time and no start fee are published; no pricing/terms/changelog page exists (all 404).

fleet.verification: Public preview no credit card required.
fleet.notes: Free public preview, future posted compute rates not yet live. Thousands of RL episodes is a scaling claim, not new-account concurrency. Quota increase process and screening unknown.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: Set auto_pause to true if you want Leap0 to pause the sandbox when its timeout is reached.
snapshot_auto.note: Opt-in per sandbox (auto_pause=true at create/restore; default false). Trigger = wall-clock timeout (max 8 h), not idle. Pause captures memory+disk ('The VM state, memory, and disk are captured and uploaded'); paused sandbox resumes automatically on the next request. Without auto_pause the sandbox is killed at timeout. Plain stop/start keeps disk only.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Snapshots let you create a point-in-time capture of a running sandbox, including its in-memory execution state and writable disk state.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Memory included. Named snapshots; 'You can then restore that snapshot into a brand new sandbox that starts from the same checkpoint.' (fork). Only from running sandboxes; optional kill_sandbox_after. Manual pause() also exists.

harness_api.quote: You can either bake it into a template or install it at runtime using
harness_api.note: Guides for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode only install the CLI and run it via the generic process.execute exec API; no first-party harness/session API. MCP server (@leap0/mcp) lets external MCP clients drive sandboxes, which is the reverse direction.

egress_allowlist.quote: Traffic is filtered by allow_domains, allow_cidrs, and optional transforms.
egress_allowlist.note: network_policy modes allow-all (default), deny-all, custom (allow_domains + allow_cidrs). Set at create/restore; persisted with snapshots. Enforced host-side per Firecracker VM.

egress_http_rules.quote: Transforms let you inject or strip headers on a per-domain basis.
egress_http_rules.note: Only HTTP-level feature is per-domain header inject/strip (TLS-terminating for transform domains). No method/path/header filtering rules documented; policy fields are only allow_domains, allow_cidrs, transforms.

ingress_rules.quote: A presigned URL is a temporary public hostname that routes traffic to a specific port inside a sandbox.
ingress_rules.note: Default invoke URL https://sbx-<id>[-port].<domain> is used with the org API key in the authorization header per docs examples; presigned URLs give tokenized, expiring (expires_in), revocable public access to one port. No IP allowlists documented.

guest_firewall.quote: Every sandbox runs in its own Firecracker microVM
guest_firewall.note: Firecracker microVM, own Linux 6.1 kernel; Docker/k3s/systemd templates imply root. Not explicitly documented.

secret_proxy.quote: This is useful for credential brokering: the sandbox code makes requests without API keys, and the firewall injects the credentials on the host side. The secrets never enter the sandbox.
secret_proxy.note: Per-domain header injection for any domain via network_policy.transforms; firewall terminates TLS only for transform domains using a per-sandbox CA. HTTP(S) only. Object-storage mounts likewise keep S3 credentials outside the guest (s3fs). No DB/SSH/git coverage documented.

volume_shared.quote: Leap0 mounts the bucket inside the sandbox with s3fs without exposing the storage credentials in the sandbox.
volume_shared.note: First-party mount of a customer-owned S3-compatible bucket (s3fs), read-write or read_only, add/edit/delete at runtime; the same bucket can be mounted in several sandboxes (not explicitly stated as a shared-volume feature, and s3fs has no strong consistency).

nested_virt.quote: Each sandbox runs in its own Firecracker microVM with a dedicated Linux kernel. The VMM process is jailed with chroot, cgroup v2, seccomp filters, and unique UID/GID pairs.
nested_virt.note: No mention of /dev/kvm or nested virtualization anywhere in the full API/SDK docs. Firecracker microVMs do not expose hardware virtualization extensions to the guest by default and Leap0 documents no opt-in for it.

anti_bot.quote: The runtime is based on Ubuntu 22.04 with an XFCE4 desktop at 1440x900 resolution. Firefox ESR, Google Chrome, and VS Code are pre-installed.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Leap0 is a general coding-agent sandbox (code interpreter + desktop/computer-use) with a plain Chrome/Firefox install, not a scraping/anti-detect browser product; no stealth or fingerprint-evasion feature is documented.

captcha_solving.quote: The runtime is based on Ubuntu 22.04 with an XFCE4 desktop at 1440x900 resolution. Firefox ESR, Google Chrome, and VS Code are pre-installed.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No CAPTCHA-solving API or service is documented anywhere in the Leap0 API/SDK reference; it is a general sandbox runtime, not a scraping/CAPTCHA product.

egress_ip_type.quote: Control what a sandbox can reach over the network using the `network_policy` field when creating or restoring a sandbox.
egress_ip_type.note: derived: sandboxes are Firecracker microVMs run on Leap0's own cloud infrastructure ("Sandboxes currently run in the US"); no residential/mobile egress product is mentioned anywhere, so outbound traffic is ordinary datacenter IP space.

fork_running.quote: Snapshots can only be created from a `running` sandbox. The VM is briefly paused during the capture and then resumed automatically unless you set `kill_sandbox_after`. ... You can then restore that snapshot into a brand new sandbox that starts from the same checkpoint.
fork_running.note: Taking a snapshot only briefly pauses the source VM (auto-resumes) and the snapshot can be restored into a brand-new independent sandbox, i.e. a running sandbox can be cloned into a new one without being stopped.

volume_attach.quote: A sandbox can attach up to 8 object storage mounts.
volume_attach.note: Object storage (S3-compatible bucket) mounts are attachable/detachable at runtime as extra persistent storage beyond the fixed 10 GiB local disk; there is no separate block-volume product, but this satisfies attachable extra persistent volumes.

auto_stop_idle.quote: Set auto_pause to true if you want Leap0 to pause the sandbox when its timeout is reached.
auto_stop_idle.note: The sandbox `timeout` is a fixed wall-clock deadline set at create/restore time (1 min - 8 h, default 5 min), not an idle-activity detector; there is no idle-detection based auto-stop.

live_resize.quote: Compute settings come from the snapshot, not the restore request.
live_resize.note: not offered: vCPU/RAM are set only at sandbox create time (or inherited from a snapshot on restore); the API reference documents no endpoint to change vCPU/RAM of a running sandbox in place.

agent_harnesses.quote: You can either bake it into a template or install it at runtime using `process.execute`.
agent_harnesses.note: Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode guides all show manually installing the CLI via the process API or baking a custom template yourself; Leap0 ships no ready-made agent-harness template (only `system/code-interpreter` and `system/desktop` are first-party templates).

own_agent_api.quote: Leap0 is primarily offered as a fully managed service with the option to bring your own compute (BYOC).
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Leap0 is sandbox/VM infrastructure (compute, filesystem, git, process, desktop/computer-use APIs) for running your own agents; it has no first-party browser/research/computer-use agent of its own that it exposes via API.

lang_node.quote: `typescript`, `ts`, `javascript`, `js`, `bun`, `node` | Bun v1.3.10 (TypeScript) | Last expression is returned as a result. State accumulates across calls.
lang_node.note: The Code Interpreter template supports JS/TypeScript execution out of the box via a Bun runtime, alongside Python.

public_ipv4.quote: A presigned URL is a temporary public hostname that routes traffic to a specific port inside a sandbox.
public_ipv4.note: Inbound access is exposed through Leap0-managed hostnames/presigned URLs (a gateway/reverse-proxy model), not a dedicated public IPv4 address per sandbox; no public IPv4 assignment is documented.

static_egress_ip.quote: Control what a sandbox can reach over the network using the `network_policy` field when creating or restoring a sandbox.
static_egress_ip.note: The firewall docs describe allow/deny domain and CIDR based egress policy only; no fixed/static outbound IP address feature is mentioned anywhere in the docs.

gpu.quote: Sandboxes currently run in the US. More regions are planned.
gpu.note: not offered: outside the product's scope for now. No GPU machine type, GPU pricing, or GPU template is mentioned anywhere on the site or docs; card's own gpu_types is empty.

arm64.quote: Each sandbox runs in its own Firecracker microVM with a dedicated Linux kernel.
arm64.note: No ARM/aarch64 architecture option is mentioned anywhere in the docs, pricing, or templates; the runtime and Docker examples (e.g. amd64-oriented base images) imply x86_64 only.

open_source.quote: Leap0 is primarily offered as a fully managed service with the option to bring your own compute (BYOC). However, it can also be deployed on your own infrastructure.
open_source.note: Self-hosting/BYOC is offered commercially ("contact our sales team"), but that is not the same as the core sandbox platform being open source; no OSI-licensed repo for the core engine is published (only client SDKs).

soc2.quote: Leap0 is free to use during the public preview period.
soc2.note: not offered: no SOC 2 attestation, security/trust page, or compliance page exists (leap0.dev/security and /trust both 404); a free public-preview product with no published compliance page.

hipaa.quote: Leap0 is free to use during the public preview period.
hipaa.note: not offered: no HIPAA/BAA mention anywhere on the site or docs; no compliance/security page exists (404s).

sso.quote: API keys authenticate all requests to the Leap0 API. Each key is scoped to an organization and grants full access to sandboxes, templates, and snapshots within that organization.
sso.note: Authentication docs describe organization-scoped API keys only; no SAML/OIDC single sign-on is mentioned anywhere in the docs or on the site.

eu_data_residency.quote: Sandboxes currently run in the US. More regions are planned.
eu_data_residency.note: Only a US region exists today; EU (or any other) region is explicitly future/roadmap, not currently available.

windows.quote: Every sandbox runs in its own Firecracker microVM: ... Sandboxes run on the Linux 6.1 LTS kernel.
windows.note: Leap0 sandboxes are Firecracker microVMs that only boot a Linux 6.1 LTS guest kernel; no Windows guest OS option exists anywhere in the docs (the one 'Windows' mention is about APPDATA in a locally-printed CLI config, not a guest OS).

macos.quote: Every sandbox runs in its own Firecracker microVM: ... Sandboxes run on the Linux 6.1 LTS kernel.
macos.note: Firecracker microVMs cannot boot a macOS guest, and Leap0's docs only describe the Linux 6.1 LTS kernel guest; no macOS support is offered or mentioned anywhere in the docs/homepage.

usage_api.quote: Leap0 API is the core platform API for creating and managing sandboxes. Use it to manage sandbox lifecycle, object storage mounts, filesystems, git, processes, PTY sessions, LSP, SSH, snapshots, templates, and presigned URLs. No usage or billing endpoint documented.
usage_api.note: granularity: none; cost: no; The full API documentation (llms-full.txt) comprehensively lists all available endpoints and SDKs: Leap0 API, Code Interpreter API, Desktop API, Metadata Service API, and various client libraries. No 'usage', 'billing', 'cost', or 'metrics' API endpoint exists. OpenTelemetry metrics are sandbox-local resource monitoring (CPU, memory, disk), not billable usage tracking. Billing has not gone live; no cost API can exist yet.

locations_quote: Sandboxes currently run in the US. More regions are planned.
